clue.text: Musical article by expert of little weight

parts.note: the definite article
a wizard is an expert, a whizz at something
taken as written
oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written by a specialist who carries no clout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like an adjective describing the article, but it is the definition: the 1939 film musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The Judy Garland film is one of the best-known screen musicals.

clue.text: Timber bench with no front going into boiler

parts.note: teak is a hardwood timber

indicators.note: the bench word loses its opening letter, its front

parts.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

explanation.surface: Wood from a bench, missing its front, gets fed into a furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: A SETTLE is an old wooden bench with a high back; 'with no front' drops its S to leave ETTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle is a vessel for boiling water, so a boiler in the kitchen sense.

clue.text: Writer's coming-out I missed

indicators.note: the I of the clue is left out, missed from the word

parts.note: emersion is the act of emerging or coming out

explanation.surface: An author regrets not being present at someone's coming-out.
explanation.walkthrough: EMERSION, an emerging, loses its I to give the American essayist Ralph Waldo Emerson.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Hearing aids reportedly behind the times?

indicators.note: what is described is said out loud and heard as another phrase

parts.note: the inner ears are the organs that aid our hearing

explanation.surface: Deaf aids that are said to be old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner ears help us hear; said aloud, 'inner ears' passes for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being late with payments leaves you behind, the question mark admitting 'the times' is a stretch.

clue.text: A nagging trouble — with heart failure?

definitions.text: A nagging trouble — with heart failure?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order
the central letters of nagging fail, dropping out

explanation.surface: A persistent ailment that might come with a failing heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with heart failure' drops the central GG from NAGGING, leaving NAING, which 'trouble' rearranges after A. The whole clue also describes the chest pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain from poor blood supply to the heart muscle, a persistent cardiac complaint.

clue.text: To blazes with a normal means for lifting fish such as these?

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the letters so they read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sod it means to blazes with it, a curse
taken as written
a rod is the normal means of landing a fish

explanation.surface: Someone cursing the usual tackle used to haul up a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: SOD + A + ROD gives SODAROD; 'for lifting' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorados are golden game fish, also called mahi-mahi.

clue.text: Tale of a bleak tree-felling

indicators.note: felling a tree removes it, so the tree OAK is cut out of the words before it

parts.note: the letters from which the tree is removed; that the tale also runs unbroken inside these words is a coincidence, since no indicator signals it

explanation.surface: A story about cutting down trees on a bleak hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the tree, OAK, from the letters of 'of a bleak' and the tale is left standing; the letters happen also to run unbroken inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short moral story, often with animal characters.

clue.text: Lots poorly in Jerusalem

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other

parts.note: Zion is a name for Jerusalem
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: Many people are sick in the holy city.
explanation.definitionFit: A zillion is an informal huge number, so a great many.

clue.text: Rising from 7, girl leaves spineless fellow

indicators.note: the girl's name departs from the word for 7, removed from it

parts.note: the answer to 7 down

indicators.note: in a down clue the name reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Liz is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl walks out on a gutless man.
explanation.walkthrough: LIZ reversed by 'Rising' is ZIL, which leaves ZILLION (7 down). The fellow is the Cowardly Lion from Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cowardly Lion in The Wizard of Oz lacks courage, which is what spineless means.

clue.text: Alias conceals the Spanish group leader

indicators.note: the alias word holds the other inside it

parts.note: aka stands for also known as, an alias
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A false name hides the identity of a Spanish ringleader.
explanation.walkthrough: Akela is the adult leader of a Cub Scout pack, named after the wolf in Kipling's Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela heads a Cub Scout pack, a group of young scouts.

clue.text: Soldier arresting a vulgar revolutionary

indicators.note: the soldier holds the other pieces, arresting them

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
taken as written
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A soldier detains a crude rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Garibaldi was the 19th-century leader of Italian unification; also a British biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the Italian revolutionary Redshirts.

clue.text: Cherished dinners he cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters being doctored or worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: He made dinners that were much loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enshrined is held sacred, treasured as if in a shrine.

clue.text: Ebbing green water

indicators.note: ebbing means flowing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive

explanation.surface: Green water receding from the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Evian is a brand of French bottled mineral water.

clue.text: "Blotke" is a heartless fellow

parts.note: the made-up word is bloke with a T placed in it, and a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A strange name is given to a callous person.
explanation.walkthrough: The made-up word shows T in BLOKE, and a bloke is a man: T IN MAN. The Tin Man in The Wizard of Oz wants a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Man of Oz has no heart and goes in search of one.

clue.text: Alienate sergeant on the march

indicators.note: marching sets the letters moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Turn a sergeant against you while marching.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to make someone unfriendly or distant, to drive them away.

clue.text: Get lost regularly with this driver?

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A golfer telling someone where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Els is a South African golfer; a driver is a golf club and here one who drives the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Els, the South African golfer, hits tee shots, so he is a driver of balls.

clue.text: Plant Dame among crowd (one at opening of Aladdin)

indicators.note: the honour sits inside the crowd word

parts.note: a ruck is a crowd or throng
a DBE (Dame Commander of the British Empire) is the honour making a woman a Dame
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A pantomime dame in the crowd during the first scene of Aladdin.
explanation.walkthrough: DBE is the British honour of a Dame; a pantomime dame is a man in drag in a Christmas show such as Aladdin.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudbeckia is a genus of daisy-like garden flowers, the coneflowers.

clue.text: Women tend to stimulate talent

indicators.note: stimulating stirs things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Women are inclined to excite people.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a natural gift or ability.

clue.text: Mortgagees short of capital squeeze American customers

indicators.note: the trimmed word squeezes the other inside it
the word loses its capital, its first letter

parts.note: mortgagees are the lenders of a mortgage

explanation.surface: Banks lacking funds put pressure on their American clients.
explanation.walkthrough: LENDERS short of its capital L gives ENDERS, which squeezes US.
explanation.definitionFit: End users are the final buyers or consumers of a product.

clue.text: Kansas girl's affair with novelist Hardy's ending

parts.note: a do is a party or affair
Philip Roth was an American novelist

indicators.note: the final letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: A woman from Kansas has a fling with a writer at the end of a Hardy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy Gale, the heroine of The Wizard of Oz, comes from Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy, heroine of The Wizard of Oz, is swept away from her Kansas farm.

clue.text: Composer's godforsaken rubbish in midst of suite

indicators.note: forsaken by a god: D, from Deus, the Latin for god, leaves the word

parts.note: dross means waste or rubbish
taken as written

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A composer calls trash written in the middle of a suite dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: DROSS loses D (from Deus, god) to give ROSS; then IN, and I from the middle of SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Trend reversed by education and cleaned up

indicators.note: the trend word is turned round, written backwards

parts.note: a tide is a trend or current of opinion

explanation.surface: A trend in education was reversed and tidied away.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited text has been corrected and tidied, cleaned up for publication.

clue.text: Divided, a party was a danger to 18

parts.note: torn means split or divided
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A split party proved hazardous to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is Dorothy, whose Kansas house is carried off to Oz by a twister.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister whirled Dorothy's house off to Oz, so it threatened her.

clue.text: Snarled and snarled at Glyn

indicators.note: to snarl is to knot up, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog growls angrily at a man called Glyn.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Snarled' is the definition in its knotted sense; the second is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangly is knotted and twisted, just as snarled thread is.

clue.text: Search crypt or chancel for illumination

indicators.note: searching inside these words turns up the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Look in the church's crypt or chancel for some light.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashlight or flaming brand gives light, so a source of illumination.

clue.text: 18's little friend's a mite old

parts.note: a tot or mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone's young companion is a small, elderly child.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is Dorothy; her little friend is her dog in the Oz story.
explanation.definitionFit: Toto is Dorothy's small dog, her constant companion in Oz.

clue.text: "Greetings, Mrs Sharples" (said to be an unprepossessing creature)

indicators.note: what is said aloud is heard as another word

parts.note: hi is a greeting and Ena was Mrs Sharples's first name

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to a soap character and is told she is unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena Sharples was a formidable gossip in the British TV soap Coronation Street; 'Hi, Ena' said aloud gives the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The scavenging, laughing carnivore is famously unlovely to look at.

clue.text: Brainless fellow cowers trembling around saloon?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit around the car word
shaking sends the letters into a new order

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car

explanation.surface: A fool shakes with fear around the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' looks like a bar but is a type of car. The Scarecrow of Oz goes in search of a brain, hence brainless.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scarecrow of Oz has a head of straw and longs for a brain.

clue.text: Jack ties knot with left inclined girl

parts.note: kn is the abbreviation for knot, the nautical speed unit

indicators.note: leaning to the left means the name is read leftwards, backwards

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man ties a knot with a girl who leans to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: In cards a jack is also called a knave.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the old name for the jack in a pack of cards.

clue.text: Happening on Thursday night and with monotonous regularity

explanation.surface: Something that happens every Thursday night, without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared at the end of 2009, when New Year's Eve, the night one year comes in as another goes out, fell on a Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: On that Thursday's New Year's Eve the year changed over; as an idiom the phrase means constantly, every year without change.
